jobs.occupation: Software Engineer (C++)
jobs.description:
Want to build C++ software that helps power the next generation of autonomous and unmanned systems?At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our technology brings together computer vision, C++ software, autonomy, embedded systems and real-world product development.

We are looking for a C++ Software Engineer to join our engineering team and contribute to the software that connects and powers different parts of Robotto’s technology platform.This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys building reliable systems, solving complex technical problems and seeing their software move beyond development into real-world operation.

The role
You will develop and maintain C++ software across Robotto’s software ecosystem, working on applications and services that support the operation, communication and coordination of our unmanned systems.Depending on the project, your work may span different parts of our platform—from software running alongside our autonomous systems to applications used to configure, control and interact with them.You will work closely with engineers across computer vision, autonomy, embedded software, electronics and testing to develop new capabilities, integrate components and continuously improve the reliability and performance of our systems.

What you will do

• 
Design, develop and maintain high-quality software primarily in C++.

• 
Build software used across our drone and unmanned-systems platform.

• 
Develop reliable communication and data flows between different software and hardware components.

• 
Work on performance-sensitive and potentially real-time or near-real-time applications.

• 
Integrate software with APIs, networking components, sensors and wider system infrastructure.

• 
Debug complex issues across interconnected software systems and identify root causes.

• 
Contribute to software architecture and technical design decisions.

• 
Write maintainable, testable and well-structured production code.

• 
Participate in code reviews, testing, documentation and continuous improvement of our engineering practices.

• 
Collaborate closely with computer vision, embedded, autonomy and hardware engineers.

• 
Support integration and testing on real systems and drone platforms..

What success could look like in your first 3–6 months

• 
You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto’s software architecture and how the different parts of our platform work together.

• 
You are contributing production-quality C++ code to our products.

• 
You have taken ownership of features or components from development through integration and testing.

• 
You are successfully debugging and solving issues across interconnected systems.

• 
You are contributing to improved reliability, maintainability and performance of our software.

• 
You have become a trusted technical partner within the engineering team.

What we are looking forWe are looking for a strong software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems and building software that interacts with real systems.

• 
Strong professional experience developing production-quality software in C++, with a solid understanding of modern software engineering practices.

• 
Solid understanding of software architecture, data structures, algorithms and object-oriented design.

• 
Experience developing multi-component or distributed software systems.

• 
Experience with networking, inter-process communication, APIs or communication protocols is highly relevant.

• 
Good understanding of concurrency, multithreading and performance considerations in C++.

• 
Experience with debugging, testing, version control and modern software development practices.

• 
Experience with Linux-based development environments is an advantage.

• 
Experience with robotics, drones, autonomous systems, defence technology or other complex technical products is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• 
Experience working with software that interfaces with hardware or real-world systems is an advantage.

• 
Professional fluency in English.

• 
A degree in computer science, software engineering, robotics or a related field is preferred; equivalent practical experience is equally welcome.

Please apply even if you don't meet every single point. We are interested in what you can bring to the team, your ability to learn and your motivation to work on the challenges we are solving.

Who you are
Beyond your technical or professional experience, we care about how you work and collaborate.You:

• 
Are curious and enjoy solving complex problems.

• 
Take ownership and follow things through.

• 
Communicate openly about progress, challenges and risks.

• 
Are comfortable in a growing company where priorities can evolve.

• 
Enjoy collaborating with people across different disciplines.

• 
Value testing, learning and continuous improvement.

• 
Want to contribute rather than simply execute a predefined set of tasks.

Why join Robotto?
Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision, autonomy and real-world operations.You will be joining Robotto at an exciting stage of our journey as we continue to grow our team, technology and products.

Our teams work across software, computer vision, control, electronics, hardware and real-world testing. This means you will work closely with people from different technical disciplines and see how your work contributes to the wider product.

We are an ambitious and collaborative team, and we value people who take ownership, challenge ideas constructively and want to help build both great technology and a great company.This is not a role where everything is already defined. You will have the opportunity to:

• 
Work on challenging technology with real-world applications.

• 
Have meaningful ownership and influence over your area.

• 
Work closely with talented colleagues across multiple disciplines.

• 
See your work move from an idea or prototype into real-world use.

• 
Help shape how we work as the company continues to grow.

Our hiring process
We want our hiring process to be straightforward, transparent and conversational.

1. Introductory conversation with People & Culture
A chance for us to learn more about you and for you to learn more about Robotto, the role and what we are looking for.

2. Meeting with the Hiring Manager
A deeper conversation about your experience, skills and approach to the role

.3. Technical / Role-specific discussion
Depending on the position, this may include a technical discussion, practical exercise, case or live scenario relevant to the work you would be doing at Robotto.

4. Leadership meeting
A conversation with a member of our leadership team to explore mutual fit and give you another opportunity to learn about Robotto and where we are going

.5. Offer
If there is a strong mutual fit, we will move forward with an offer.The exact process may vary slightly depending on the role.

Interested?
If this sounds like an opportunity you would like to explore, we would love to hear from you.Apply through our careers page and tell us a little about yourself, your experience and why Robotto interests you.

Equal opportunity
At Robotto, we want to build a team where different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives are valued.We welcome applications from qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, nationality, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or other characteristics protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Electrical and Computer Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD Position in Physical AI: Adaptive Foundation Models for Robotics

Research area and project description
Applications are invited for a three-year PhD position in Physical AI at Aarhus University's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The candidate will join the Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, supervised by Associate Professor Behzad Bozorgtabar and co-supervised by Professor Qi Zhang.

Research vision
How can intelligent robots understand instructions, anticipate the consequences of actions, and adapt reliably when the physical world changes? The project connects multimodal perception, reasoning and action with predictive learning and edge intelligence.

Research directions and objectives

Vision-language-action models (VLAs)
Investigate VLA models and multimodal representations that connect visual observations and language instructions to robot behaviour, including learning from demonstrations and generalisation to unfamiliar tasks, objects or environments.

World models and planning
Develop models that predict how the physical world responds to actions, supporting planning and learning from interaction. Possible directions include learning from video, demonstrations and simulation, and transferring knowledge across robot configurations.

Adaptation and edge intelligence
Develop efficient methods for maintaining reliable behaviour under changing environments, sensing conditions and resource constraints. Topics may include test-time and continual adaptation, uncertainty-aware decision-making, and efficient inference and model updates under latency, memory and energy limits.

The precise research focus will be developed with the successful candidate within these connected directions. Research will emphasise new learning algorithms and rigorous evaluation using public datasets, simulation and, where available, robotic and edge-computing platforms. Evaluation will consider task success, generalisation, reliability and computational efficiency. The goal is original research for leading machine-learning, computer-vision and robotics venues. The successful candidate will be expected to conduct original, high-quality research targeting publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision and robotics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, CoRL, RSS and ICRA.

Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Essential qualifications
A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent), completed by enrolment, in computer science, electrical or computer engineering, robotics, machine learning or a related field; strong academic results and foundations in machine learning, linear algebra, probability and optimisation; and strong Python and PyTorch (or comparable framework) skills.

Only applicants who demonstrate substantial hands-on experience implementing, training and evaluating deep-learning models will be considered. General interest in AI or experience limited to running tutorials or using pretrained-model APIs is not sufficient.

Applicants must provide evidence of research potential through a substantial thesis, research project, code contribution or publication, clearly identifying their own technical contribution.

Desirable experience
Research experience in multimodal foundation models or robot learning is particularly desirable, especially involving vision–language–action models or world models. Experience in model adaptation or efficient edge deployment is an additional advantage. We particularly value substantial technical contributions, demonstrated through a thesis, research project, code contribution or publication. Prior publications and hands-on robotics experience are advantageous but not required.

Application and selection
Include a one-page statement of interest identifying relevant research directions and your strongest technical project; a CV with a project portfolio and publications, where applicable; and Bachelor's and Master's transcripts and diplomas, as available. Provide links or an accessible description of relevant code, methods and results, and explain your personal contribution.

Shortlisted applicants should be prepared to discuss their own implementation, experimental design, results and limitations in a technical interview. Clear scientific communication in English and a commitment to reproducible research are essential.

Use the project description from this announcement; a separate research proposal is not required.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), Faculty of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Finlandsgade 22, 8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

• Qi Zhang, qz@ece.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Auditing
jobs.description:
The Department of Accounting invites applications for a PhD position in Auditing. The Department of Accounting is one of the oldest and largest accounting departments in Europe. We have a growing and flourishing research environment within financial accounting, management accounting and control, auditing, and corporate governance.

We especially welcome PhD proposals that adopt qualitative research methods and suggest novel approaches to the study of

• The making of the audit profession, especially regarding emerging technologies in auditing, such as generative artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on how they may reshape the audit profession, including the training and socialization of auditors, the exercise of professional judgment and the relevance of the traditional audit model in responding to evolving societal demands.
• Audit firm ownership, including the emerging role of private equity firms acquiring ownership interests in audit firms. Proposals within this research theme may explore implications for, for example, the partnership model, audit firm governance, how audits are conducted, talent management, client portfolios, audit market competition, and how these developments may reconfigure the audit profession.
• The role of auditing and assurance in sustainable development. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to explore alternative forms of auditing and assurance that contribute to sustainable development and to propose empirical work that goes beyond simply examining the current compliance-oriented role associated with the verification of sustainability reports. Proposals should aim to develop research that provides a basis for debate about how auditing and assurance can play a meaningful role in sustainability.
• Regulator-auditor interaction, with a focus on challenges and potential pathways in public oversight practices, including, for example, the role of firm-level oversight practices and dialogue, as well as the role of ad hoc regulatory investigations alongside routine quality inspections.
• Client-auditor interaction, with a focus on, for example, the governance role of audit committees, the negotiation of accounting issues, professional and commercial conflicts, or the role of client technology adoption in the performance of audits.
• Auditing in the context of audit firm organization and governance, with the aim of understanding how increasingly intensive and sophisticated audit firm-level systems (e.g., quality management, incentive systems, performance measurement, and culture/tone at the top) operate to manage and control auditor behavior within audit firms. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to propose research that can inform reflections on how bureaucracy in audit firms can be balanced, how tendencies toward defensive behavior might be reversed, and how professional judgment at all levels, from junior auditors to partners, might be encouraged.
The project should speak to contemporary concerns in auditing and aim to contribute to academic, public, professional, and company-level debates. The PhD project should therefore be informed and enriched by engagement with firms and professionals as part of both the research process and the dissemination of research findings, and we encourage proposals to demonstrate the potential for such engagement.

The PhD position is based in the Department of Accounting, and the candidate will be part of the department’s auditing research group. We welcome applicants with degrees or experience in accounting and auditing. We also welcome applicants from other social sciences who are interested in engaging with auditing as a research domain. The auditing research group consists of researchers with backgrounds in accounting and auditing, as well as researchers from other academic fields who have a strong interest in auditing. The PhD candidate will work in close collaboration with the supervisors and benefit from the international research environment in the Department of Accounting and at CBS. Candidates are encouraged to contact Professor Thomas Riise Johansen (trj.acc@cbs.dk) for informal discussions and information about the position before submitting the application.

About the PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant will show an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/acc

Application and admission requirements
The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must:

• have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)
• have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale (https://ufm.dk/en/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system)
• have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted. In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.
• have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS
• master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking
The application (see link below) must include a five-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed empirical material
• a work plan for the three years
More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmemes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts
• documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met)
• a concise curriculum vitae (CV)

The PhD position is a non-tenured full-time position of 3 years, with teaching and course work obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The PhD project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

Applications are invited for one or more fully funded PhD scholarships at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark, Odense.

Depending on academic qualifications, applicants may be enrolled in either the 4+4 or the 5+3 PhD programme. Both programmes include a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offer a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January  2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within four research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; and Microeconomics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Historical Economics and Development Group (HEDG), which focuses on Economic History with a strong emphasis on applied microeconomics and causal inference. HEDG is internationally acknowledged as a leading research group and attracts substantial grants and media coverage, as well as publishing books and articles with top outlets.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professor Anthony Wray on Private Foundations, a Carlsberg Foundation-funded project on the roles of private investment and medical education in shaping innovation and inequality in the United States during the early twentieth century. For further information about the project, please see this link.

These are applied microeconomic questions in health, labour, education, and demographic economics, approached with historical data. We are interested in strong applied microeconomists broadly, not only in candidates who already identify as economic historians, and there is scope for the PhD student to develop their own questions within the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, including independent, single-authored work. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Anthony Wray and will join a research group that includes two postdoctoral researchers and scientific research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

The project has its own GPU environment — university hardware, reserved for this project and its research team. It runs open-weight models locally for large-scale digitisation and data extraction from historical sources, alongside frontier models. We are also building an autonomous workflow for agentic-supported academic research, and the PhD student will have the chance to help develop that workflow.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Qualified candidates currently enrolled in a relevant master’s programme are also welcome to apply. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid knowledge of econometrics and applied quantitative methods, with experience using Python, R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and in cooperation with a PhD supervisor.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, machine learning, large language models, and natural language processing.

• 
Experience working with large datasets and conducting empirical research. 

• 
Demonstrated interest in economic history or cultural economics.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Successful applicants are expected to contribute to the development of academic programs and the research community. Applicants should have a PhD in Power Electronics or a closely related field. 

The DHFE section focuses on conducting research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communication, utilizing cutting-edge reconfigurable computing and sensors. The aim is to develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions that solve technology-related challenges in fields such as autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grid, and healthcare.

Applicants are expected to establish and maintain a research program in high-frequency power electronics and power management for computation, along with low-voltage electronic systems. The position emphasizes converter and power-management for computing platforms and resource-constrained applications, including battery-operated, energy-harvesting, mobile, autonomous, embedded, and sensor-based systems.

The section is a vital component of our Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Science, and Master of Science programs in Electrical and Electronics Engineering in Odense. Currently, the section focuses on three research fields: 1) Drones for Infrastructure Inspections and Interactions, 2) High-Frequency SMPS and power management for low-power electronic systems, and 3) Telecommunication Systems. The section has 15 academics, including professors, postdoctoral fellows, PhD students, and engineers, to support research, industrial collaboration, and educational activities, and is growing steadily.

The SDU campus in Odense contains six faculties and soon a large university hospital, creating a great concentration of academics and students facilitating interdisciplinary research and rich student life. The city of Odense is culturally rich, surrounded by a vibrant and growing robotics community, and highly livable with a green-banked meandering river cutting through the centre and attractive residential areas.

 

Job Description

The position focuses on power management for resource-constrained autonomous, mobile, and embedded electronic systems. Relevant research areas include high-frequency power conversion, battery-operated systems, energy harvesting, power management architectures, embedded control, and analog/digital control of converters. The application domain spans from ultra-low-power electronics and sensors to mobile platforms, robotics, drones, IoT devices, and power management for embedded, compact, and high-performance computing systems.

The role strengthens DHFE’s research profile at the interface between power electronics, microelectronics, embedded systems, and intelligent electronic devices. It is expected to support shared research themes across SDU, including energy-efficient electronics, autonomous systems, battery-powered platforms, sensor networks, health technology, and miniaturized or distributed devices.

The successful candidate should work constructively both with colleagues within DHFE and also with colleagues from other research units, such as SDU Microelectronics, SDU Centre for Industrial Electronics, the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, Faculty of Health (specifically Health Tech), Mechanical Engineering, and other relevant environments, translating power electronics competence into system-level contributions for electronic devices and platforms.

 

Duties

As a faculty member, you will be responsible for developing and delivering undergraduate and graduate teaching in Electronic and Electrical Engineering, with particular attention to strengthening control and power electronics within the BSc portfolio. This includes supervising students at Bachelor and Master’s level, mentoring students, integrating with the student body, and participating in education and outreach activities. Research duties include establishing an externally funded research agenda, publishing in leading journals and conferences, supervising early-career researchers, and contributing to the development of DHFE’s research environment. The candidate is also expected to contribute to external collaboration and perform service at the section, department, university, and professional levels.

 

Qualifications Required

• 
The applicant should hold a doctoral degree (PhD) in Power Electronics, Electronics, or a related subject area. 

• 
Demonstrated potential for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses at the university level. 

• 
The applicant must have relevant research expertise in areas related to efficient and high-frequency power converters, converter control, and power management for computing or embedded electronic systems.

• 
The applicant must have teaching skills that align with the content and responsibilities of the position. This includes possessing both pedagogical and professional skills essential for carrying out the tasks associated with the role.

jobs.occupation: Tracking & Webanalytics Specialist
jobs.description:
Do you get a small, slightly nerdy kick out of working out why a conversion stopped firing three weeks ago and nobody noticed?

At Helion B2B we don't just "run ads" for our clients. We build data-driven growth engines for some of the most ambitious B2B companies in Europe. But an engine is only as good as its sensors. That's where you come in.

You won't just keep the engine running. You'll help build it.

You'll join our tracking team in Aarhus, working day to day with our Tracking Lead. Real ownership early, someone who has done all of it sitting right next to you, and a direct hand in how the practice develops. We have standards, and we like them being challenged. If you think we're doing something the hard way, we'd rather hear it in week two than in year two.

You'll work across all of it: new implementations, server-side setups, multi-market containers, consent, QA, troubleshooting, and the measurement plans that hold it together. Real clients, and real responsibility for whether their measurement holds up.

Some of that is building something new. A lot of it is taking a setup that already exists and making it better than you found it, which is where data quality actually comes from. Your scope over the clients you look after grows from there.

The job doesn't stop when the data arrives. Part of the work is reporting and analysis: helping a client see what their numbers are telling them, and noticing when a number is telling them something wrong. Mostly technical work, then, but not only

Your playground

• 
Google Tag Manager: Web containers from day one, server-side (sGTM) as you grow into it.

• 
GA4: Event design, debugging, and making sure the numbers actually mean something.

• 
HubSpot: we're an Elite HubSpot partner, so tracking data and CRM data have to meet properly.

• 
Consent management: Cookiebot and Cookie Information, Consent Mode, and the GDPR reality behind them.

• 
Data Studio and reporting: Turning all of the above into something a client can read and act on, and being able to say what it means.

• 
AI-assisted tracking: We're actively building agent-supported auditing, monitoring and insight workflows. You'll use them, break them, and help shape where they go next.

What you need on day one

• 
You can build and debug tags, triggers and variables in a web GTM container on your own. Preview mode and Tag Assistant are familiar territory.

• 
You can configure and debug GA4, and you know what to start checking when a dimension comes back as (not set).

• 
You're a finisher. "Done" means tested and verified, not deployed.

• 
You think for yourself. When you hit a wall, you research, test and come back with a proposal rather than waiting for instructions.

• 
You're curious about where AI is taking this field. You don't need experience with it. You need to want to poke at it.

Somewhere around three to five years of hands-on tracking experience, from an agency or in-house, is the usual shape. It's a guide, not a gate.

What you'll learn here

Server-side GTM and Conversions API. Consent Mode in depth. HubSpot data flows. BigQuery. Multi-market container architecture. Reporting and analysis on top of GA4 and BigQuery. B2B lead cycles, and why they make tracking a harder problem than e-commerce.

Experience with any of these is an advantage. None of them are requirements. You'll have a lead who would rather teach you properly than do it twice.

The practical bits

• 
Where: Our Aarhus office, with a minimum of three days a week on site.

• 
Language: We work in English. Danish is an advantage, not a requirement.

• 
Right to work: You must already hold the right to work in Denmark: EU/EEA citizenship, or a valid Danish work and residence permit.

• 
Everyday life: Lunch scheme and flexible hours. We care that the work lands, not that you were at your desk at 08:30.

• 
Pension and insurance: Company-paid pension and health insurance (sundhedsforsikring).

• 
Growing here: We back training and certifications, and you'll have a lead who would rather you learned something new than closed one more ticket.

• 
The social side: fredagsbar, summer party, julefrokost and a yearly off-site. If you're new to Denmark, ask about the julefrokost.

> Earlier in your career than the above, but the rest of this sounds like you? Apply anyway and tell us where you're at. We'd rather shape the level around the right person than miss them.

Business-to-business, person-to-person

Helion B2B is a fast-growing, Elite HubSpot partner that helps B2B companies build growth engines.

We are an ambitious, curious team genuinely passionate about our work. We are eager to learn, value great social relationships and are not afraid of challenging ourselves and our clients if we feel that there is a better way to solve a challenge.

 Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences

 The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN); Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as full Professor within the area of microbial interactions in plant and environmental systems.

  Research and teaching at PLEN covers topics within Agriculture, Plant Science, Biotechnology, Biosolutions and Environmental Sciences, dealing with a wide range of subjects focusing especially on plants, soil, and microorganisms from molecules through organisms to populations and anthropogenic ecosystems. It is our vision to maintain and develop our position as one of the leading departments for plant science and the related areas based on excellent basic and applied research.

  The department hosts state-of-the art infrastructure and unique field research facilities, with many opportunities for collaborations across the department. The department is organised into four sections, and the appointed professor will be affiliated to the section of Environmental Sciences located at the Frederiksberg campus.

  The section of Environmental Sciences carries out world-leading research across diverse disciplines, including soil microbiology, chemistry, agrohydrology, ecotoxicology, to assess and mitigate human impacts on ecosystems. By combining measurements, experiments, and modelling, the section supports both basic environmental science and applied solutions for sustainable agriculture, climate mitigation, and clean soil and water. The section of Environmental Sciences conducts world-leading research covering environmental biology, chemistry, and ecosystem science. Focusing on agroecosystems and impacts on soil, water, and the atmosphere, the section connects fundamental discoveries to solutions for targeting climate impacts, microbial diversity, and toxicological challenges.

  The professor is expected to teach both at the BSc and MSc levels primarily in the Biotechnology and the Natural resources and Environmental Sciences programmes at the Frederiksberg Campus and to expand these regular teaching commitments to the new MSc in Biosolutions in Kalundborg.

  Duties include the applicant’s own research, development of the field, assessment tasks, grant applications, and research management such as supervision and training of research fellows and other staff. The successful applicant must also teach, supervise, prepare and participate in examinations, and fulfill other tasks requested by the Department.

  Description of qualifications needed

  The professorship is advertised within the area of microbial solutions for climate-friendly and sustainable production systems. Full exploitation of these solutions requires basic understanding of the complex interactions in the environment which shape microbial communities and their functions in soil and at the plant root interface.

  Hence, the appointed professor should have a broad knowledge of microbial ecology including microbial functioning under soil conditions, drivers for microbiome assembly as well as microbe-microbe and plant-microbe interactions of importance for soil and plant health. It is expected that the professor has a recognized international position in the field and contributes to the design and implementation of new methodologies within microbial ecology. The successful candidate is expected to drive research within:

   	
• Model system development for causality and mechanistic understanding of microbial functioning under natural soil conditions 	
• The microbial component of N and P nutrition in agricultural systems 	
• Drivers for root colonization and microbial assembly in agricultural systems 	
• Microbial functions of importance for soil health and functioning 	
• Microbial solutions for climate mitigation and sustainable plant production   The appointed professor is expected to cover teaching in existing courses both at the MSc and BSc levels in subjects related to microbiology, molecular genetics and biotechnology. Likewise, the appointed professor is expected to be a driver for the development of courses to ensure high-quality teaching in a constantly changing educational landscape. Supervision of BSc and MSc projects is expected on a regular basis. International candidates are expected to be able to contribute actively to teaching in Danish within 3-6 years, including supervision and assessment of students. Applicants are required to have university level teaching experience, documented teaching competencies and must be able to explain and reflect upon own teaching practice and portfolio. Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme for assistant professors is required.

  The candidate should fulfil the following criteria:

   	
• PhD or similar in molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, or a related field 	
• Profound experience in the study of plant microbe-related issues in the context of sustainable agriculture 	
• An excellent publication record that includes corresponding-author, senior author and first author publications of relevance to the position and demonstrate an impact on the scientific field of microbial interactions related to soils, plants and the environment 	
• Proven leadership in an academic research environment and ability to guide an independent research group to achieve specific goals 	
• Extensive experience in the development, organization, restructuring, and management of courses at BSc and MSc levels, supported by a comprehensive teaching portfolio that documents pedagogic competences and ongoing skills development. 	
• Extensive experience with supervision of BSc, MSc, and PhD students, as well as postdocs 	
• A teaching portfolio that documents teaching experience and reflections on teaching skills 	
• Documented ability to obtain independent research grants from private and public foundations. 	
• A strong track record of successful external/international collaborations. 	
• Documented experience in organizational tasks such as departmental committees 	
• Experience with outreach activities and communication of research to the public and stakeholders via, e.g., popular science events, press releases, interviews, conferences etc 	
• Societal impact in terms of participation in appropriate stakeholder networks   Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  General criteria apply to the appointment of professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5c_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-professors.pdf
 
 Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  
 Salary and employment conditions

  The position is open from 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is as Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.   There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Further information on the department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department Morten Petersen (morten.petersen@plen.ku.dk).

  
 Filing of application
 The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  Please include

• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines

• Separate reprints of 5 particularly relevant papers    

  The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.
